headline: Graphs pair topology with auxiliary knowledge for gene and protein network inference
label: Graph Learning For Biological Networks
summary: Recent preprints and a published method pair graph topology with sequence, ontology, or pairwise features for single-cell and protein network inference.
synthesis: The common thread is decomposing relational information into separable components rather than relying on a single pooled graph. scOntoFM embeds the cell ontology hierarchy through LCA-based triplet sampling in a single-cell foundation model, improving zero-shot cell- and gene-level tasks. scGPL jointly models global regulatory graph topology and pairwise TF-target interactions for GRN inference from scRNA-seq. ProtLink combines frozen ESM-2 features with PPI topology and cross-species orthogroup edges, with HGT reaching AP 0.970 on human PPI. scAdaG2M, published in Bioinformatics, distills graph structure into an MLP via graph-to-MLP knowledge distillation with AdaBoost reweighting to reduce over-smoothing in scRNA-seq clustering. The novelty lies in pairing topology with auxiliary knowledge sources, such as ontologies, sequence embeddings, or distilled structure, rather than treating graph connectivity as the sole signal.
